title: Mental Health & Stress
objectives: Recognize signs of stress and anxiety
Know when to seek professional help
target_phrases: I need to take a break
Have you considered talking to someone?
It's okay to ask for help

dialogue.title: Managing Stress and Anxiety
dialogue.context: Ahmed talks with friends about feeling stressed. They share coping strategies and support each other.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Honestly, I've been feeling really stressed lately. Work is busy, I'm worried about money, and I miss my family.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: I'm sorry you're going through that. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed sometimes. What's stressing you most?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Mostly work. My boss wants me to work faster, but I'm still learning. I feel like I'm not good enough.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: I felt the same way when I started. You're doing great! Remember, you're still new. Don't be so hard on yourself.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: Carlos is right. Also, what helps me when I'm stressed is taking breaks. Even a five-minute walk can help.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I don't take breaks. I work through lunch because I want to prove I'm a good worker.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: That's actually making it worse! Your brain needs rest. I take a real lunch break every day, and it helps me focus better in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: I also do deep breathing exercises when I feel anxious. It sounds simple, but it really works.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I haven't tried that. What else helps you guys?

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: Exercise is huge for me. When I play soccer, I forget about my worries for a while. It releases stress.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: And talking to friends helps - like we're doing now! If stress gets really bad, though, there's no shame in seeing a counselor. Many workplaces offer free counseling through Employee Assistance Programs.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Thank you both. I feel better just talking about it. I'll try taking breaks and maybe start exercising again.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: We're here for you, man. Check in with us - let us know how you're doing. That's what friends are for.

listening_exercises.transcript: Common signs of stress include: difficulty sleeping, headaches, muscle tension, stomach problems, irritability, trouble concentrating, and feeling overwhelmed. If you experience several of these symptoms regularly, you may be dealing with chronic stress. It's important to address stress before it affects your physical health.
listening_exercises.question: What are signs of stress?
options: Difficulty sleeping, headaches, and feeling overwhelmed

listening_exercises.transcript: Healthy ways to manage stress: exercise regularly - physical activity reduces stress hormones; get enough sleep - aim for 7-9 hours; talk to someone - friends, family, or a counselor; practice mindfulness or meditation; take breaks during work; limit caffeine and alcohol; do activities you enjoy. Everyone's different, so find what works for you.
listening_exercises.question: Which is a healthy way to manage stress?

listening_exercises.transcript: When should you seek professional help? If stress or anxiety interferes with daily life, if you feel depressed for more than two weeks, if you have thoughts of harming yourself, or if coping strategies aren't helping. Therapy is not a sign of weakness - it's a smart way to take care of your mental health. Many insurance plans cover mental health services.
listening_exercises.question: When should you seek professional help?
options: When stress interferes with daily life

speaking_tasks.prompt: Describe a time you felt stressed. What was the situation? How did you handle it? Record for 30 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: Last month, I felt very stressed because I had to prepare for a big presentation at work. I was worried I would make mistakes in English. I couldn't sleep well and felt anxious all the time. To cope with the stress, I practiced my presentation many times. I also talked to my friend Lisa, and she helped me feel more confident. On the day of the presentation, I did deep breathing exercises beforehand. It went well! I learned that preparing and talking to friends really helps reduce my stress.

speaking_tasks.prompt: Give advice to a friend who's feeling overwhelmed with work and family responsibilities. Suggest 3 coping strategies. Record for 25 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: I understand feeling overwhelmed - it's really common. Here are three things that might help. First, try to take short breaks during the day, even just five or ten minutes to breathe and clear your mind. Second, talk to someone you trust about how you're feeling - sometimes just expressing your feelings helps. Third, try to get some exercise, even a short walk. And remember, it's okay to ask for help from family, friends, or a professional counselor. You don't have to handle everything alone.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write about what causes you stress and what helps you cope. Include at least 3 coping strategies. (60-80 words)
writing_tasks.example: Several things cause me stress. Work deadlines and learning new skills can be stressful. I also worry about money sometimes, and I miss my family who lives far away. To cope with stress, I use several strategies. First, I try to exercise at least three times a week - physical activity really helps me feel better. Second, I talk to my friends when I'm feeling overwhelmed. Third, I make sure to get enough sleep. I also try to take breaks during work instead of working non-stop. These strategies help me manage my stress in a healthy way.

writing_tasks.prompt: Your friend seems very stressed and won't talk about it. Write a supportive message encouraging them to open up or seek help. (50-60 words)
writing_tasks.example: Hi Carlos, I've noticed you seem stressed lately and I'm worried about you. I want you to know I'm here if you need to talk - no judgment, just support. Sometimes it helps to share what we're going through with friends. If you're not comfortable talking to me, that's okay too, but please consider talking to someone - maybe a counselor or another friend. You don't have to handle everything alone. I care about you.

grammar_focus.title: 'Feel + adjective' for Emotions
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'feel + adjective' to describe emotional states.
examples: I feel stressed. (emotional state)
She feels anxious. (emotional state)
They feel overwhelmed. (emotional state)
He feels better now. (changed state)

grammar_focus.title: 'Make/Let + object + verb' for Causation
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'make + object + verb' when something causes a feeling. Use 'let + object + verb' for permission.
examples: This makes me feel anxious. (causes the feeling)
Stress makes me tired. (causes tiredness)
Exercise makes me feel better. (causes improvement)
Let yourself rest. (give yourself permission)

grammar_focus.title: Gerunds for Activities (-ing as noun)
grammar_focus.explanation: Use gerund (verb + -ing) as a noun to talk about activities that help with stress.
examples: Talking helps me cope. (talking = activity as subject)
I enjoy exercising. (exercising = activity as object)
Walking reduces stress. (walking = activity as subject)
She's good at managing stress. (managing = activity after preposition)

vocabulary.example: Work stress is affecting my sleep.

cultural_notes: Mental health is increasingly discussed openly in the U.S., though stigma still exists in some communities.
Many U.S. workplaces offer Employee Assistance Programs (EAP) with free confidential counseling.
Therapy and counseling are becoming more normalized - about 20% of American adults see a therapist.
Mental health days - taking time off work for mental health - are becoming more accepted.
Online therapy platforms like BetterHelp and Talkspace are popular and often cheaper than in-person therapy.
The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is a free, confidential 24/7 resource for anyone in crisis.
